uutiset.t: US Plans for Tariffs Face Pushback
uutiset.s: Trading partners have responded to the latest US tariff plans with a mix of disappointment and protests, while some hold out the prospect for negotiations. Bloomberg's North Asia correspondent Minmin Low says China and the EU have made it clear that they will retaliate if necessary. (Source: Bloombe

uutiset.t: Gold Steadies as Fed Rate Path and AI Stocks Frame Volatile Week
uutiset.s: Gold steadied, as traders weighed the prospect of Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes against a wider market recovery spurred by a rebound in US technology stocks.

uutiset.t: ‘Dollar Storm:’ Greenback on Track for Longest Winning Run Since 2024
uutiset.s: The dollar is poised for its longest monthly winning streak in two years as a rupture in the artificial intelligence trade and rising interest rates spur demand for safe-haven assets.

uutiset.t: Japan Bank Shares Risk Further Unwind as Funding Cost Bites
uutiset.s: Japanese banking shares face increasing risk of an unwind as higher interest rates provide less of a boost to profits amid intensifying competition across the sector.

uutiset.t: Lula Taps Bradesco Chair as Finance Chief to Soothe Markets
uutiset.s: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva tapped Bradesco Chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi as finance minister, turning to one of Brazil’s best-known bankers to restore investor confidence in the nation’s finances.

uutiset.t: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Nov. 27
uutiset.s: Oil headed for the first weekly gain this month as attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers in the Middle East raised concerns about escalating hostilities.

uutiset.t: Bankers Pay Up for Hong Kong Apartments as Rents Hit New Highs
uutiset.s: Hong Kong’s booming rental real estate market is spurring gains in previously underappreciated neighborhoods, as bankers pay up for apartments in one of the world’s most expensive places to live.

uutiset.t: Euro Set for Biggest Drop in Two Decades Against Yuan This Year
uutiset.s: The euro is set for its biggest annual slide against the yuan in two decades, with European officials calling on China to let its currency strengthen further to curb surging imports.

uutiset.t: AI Rout Makes Kioxia Japan’s Cheapest Blue Chip, Backing Bulls
uutiset.s: The brutal selloff in Kioxia Holdings Corp. on worries over the AI boom’s sustainability has made it the cheapest Japanese blue chip, reinforcing bullish analyst calls.

uutiset.t: Asian Stocks Rise for Second Day, Crude Oil Gains: Markets Wrap
uutiset.s: Asian stocks extended their rebound as buyers returned to the artificial intelligence trade following weeks of volatility. Oil climbed after Yemen’s Houthi rebels struck a key Saudi refinery.

uutiset.t: Ford CEO on Le Mans, New Electric Pickup and Trade Talks
uutiset.s: Bloomberg’s Matt Miller sits down with Ford CEO Jim Farley to talk racing, Ford’s planned $30,000 electric pickup, Chinese EV competition and USMCA trade talks, zeroing in on how to protect US auto manufacturing while competing on a global stage. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Ghana Buys Back $1.1 Billion Domestic Bonds to Boost Confidence
uutiset.s: Ghana redeemed a four-year domestic bond three months ahead of maturity, as the government sought to bolster investor confidence in an economy recovering from a debt restructuring.

uutiset.t: New Zealand Poised to Learn Who Can Form Its Next Government
uutiset.s: New Zealand will learn Friday who is in a position to form its next government, three weeks after an election that was too close to call.

uutiset.t: KKR Banks Line Up €550 Million of Debt to Back Logoplaste Buyout
uutiset.s: Banks have lined up €550 million ($603.5 million) of loans to back KKR & Co.’s acquisition of packaging company Logoplaste, according to people familiar with the situation.

uutiset.t: Mexican Peso in Worst Losing Streak in Years on Carry Unwind
uutiset.s: The Mexican peso posted its longest losing streak in five years on Thursday as investors flee to safe haven assets and the popular carry trade unravels.
